chunks: For, by Allāh, I do not bow before you so that you may humiliate me, nor do I let loose the reins for you so that you may drive me away.
I swear by Allāh an oath wherein I, except the will of Allāh, shall so train myself that I will feel joyed if I get one loaf for eating, and be content with only salt to season it.
I shall let my eyes empty themselves of tears like the stream whose water has flown away.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's advice to the governor of Basra regarding humility and asceticism?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses the governor of Basra, urging him to maintain his dignity and not become subservient to the elite's lavish hospitality. He vows to train his soul in asceticism, finding joy in simple food like a loaf of bread with salt, and to weep until his tears are exhausted, symbolizing deep spiritual reflection and detachment from worldly excess. This passage highlights the Shia concept of *riyadat al-nafs* (disciplining the soul) as a means to preserve political and spiritual independence from corrupt power structures.
